title: Distribution of Ruin Times in Gambler's Ruin
description: Algebraic analysis of the gambler's-ruin closed forms: the ruin probabilities (k/N), expected ruin time (k(N-k)), variance, biased-walk odds-ratio formula, and the cos(π/N) decay rate are taken as definitions, and the file proves their algebraic properties (sum-to-one, bounds, symmetry, AM-GM bound, harmonic/discrete-Laplacian recurrence, biased extension). The Optional Stopping Theorem derivation that justifies these closed forms is described but not formalized here.

meta.author: Doob (1953), Feller (1968)
originalContributions: Axiom-free proof that the defined ruin probabilities sum to 1: k/N + (N-k)/N = 1 (previously axiomized)
Consistency identity for the defined ruin probabilities: P(win)·N = k (an algebraic check, not a formalized proof of the Optional Stopping Theorem)
Biased gambler's ruin structure with odds ratio formulation
Proof that unfavorable games have strictly sub-unity win probability
Exponential decay rate cos(π/N) ∈ (0,1) for ruin time distribution
Complete AM-GM bound on expected ruin time: E[T] ≤ N²/4
Harmonic property of expected ruin time (discrete Laplacian)
prerequisites: Martingale theory and the Optional Stopping Theorem
Characteristic functions and spectral analysis of Markov chains
Discrete harmonic functions and potential theory
meta.assumptions: The closed-form ruin probability (k/N), expected ruin time (k(N-k)), and biased odds-ratio formula are taken as definitional inputs; the Optional Stopping Theorem derivation that justifies them is not formalized in this file. Given those definitions, the file is fully machine-checked with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: The Gambler's Ruin problem is one of the oldest problems in probability theory, dating to correspondence between Pascal and Fermat in 1654. The modern treatment uses martingale theory developed by Doob (1953). The Optional Stopping Theorem provides the key tool: by applying it to the identity martingale X_n and the quadratic martingale X_n² - n, one extracts both ruin probabilities and expected ruin times. The biased case was analyzed by Feller (1968) using the exponential martingale r^X_n where r = q/p.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question**: What can we prove about the distribution of ruin times in the Gambler's Ruin problem?

**Answer**: For a symmetric random walk with absorbing barriers at 0 and N, starting at k:
1. P(reach N) = k/N, P(reach 0) = (N-k)/N
2. E[T] = k(N-k) (quadratic in N)
3. P(T > t) ~ C·cos(π/N)^t (exponential decay)

For biased walks (p ≠ 1/2), the odds ratio r = q/p governs everything: P(win) = (1-r^k)/(1-r^N).
overview.text: Algebraic analysis of the gambler's-ruin closed forms. The ruin probabilities, expected ruin time, variance, biased-walk formula, and cos(π/N) decay rate are taken as definitions, and the file proves their algebraic properties. The Optional Stopping Theorem derivation justifying these closed forms is described but not formalized here.
overview.proofStrategy:
Apply the Optional Stopping Theorem to different martingales:
- **Linear martingale** X_n: gives ruin probabilities P(win) = k/N
- **Quadratic martingale** X_n² - n: gives E[T] = k(N-k)
- **Exponential martingale** r^(X_n): gives biased ruin probabilities

The exponential decay rate comes from the spectral analysis of the transition matrix: the dominant eigenvalue is cos(π/N), proved to lie in (0,1) for N ≥ 3.
keyInsights: All axioms from the previous version were eliminated by proving them directly from definitions: k/N + (N-k)/N = 1 and (k/N)·N = k are pure algebra
The biased random walk introduces the odds ratio r = q/p as the fundamental parameter. When p < 1/2 (unfavorable), r > 1, and the gambler's win probability is exponentially small in N
The ruin time distribution has exponential tails governed by cos(π/N). For large N, this is approximately 1 - π²/(2N²), so the decay is very slow
Expected ruin time k(N-k) ≤ N²/4 (AM-GM), with equality when starting at the midpoint k = N/2. The poor gambler (k=1) faces linear expected time N-1
The harmonic property E[T|k] = 1 + (E[T|k-1] + E[T|k+1])/2 connects ruin times to discrete harmonic functions and potential theory

sections.title: Module Header and Overview
sections.summary: Imports, the module docstring stating the open question (quantitative gambler's-ruin / fair-games analysis via the Optional Stopping Theorem), the answer, improvements over the previous version, and the connection to the parent file.
sections.mathContext: Quantitative gambler's ruin: ruin probabilities, expected ruin time, variance, and the biased case, via Optional Stopping.

sections.title: Part I: Setup — Symmetric Random Walk with Barriers
sections.summary: Defines the `GamblersRuin` structure (absorbing barriers at 0 and N, start position k) and the quantities `ruinProbWin` (k/N), `ruinProbLose` ((N−k)/N), and `expectedRuinTime` (k(N−k)).

sections.title: Part II: Ruin Probability via the Linear Martingale
sections.summary: Applies the Optional Stopping Theorem to the linear martingale: `ost_linear`, `ruin_probabilities_sum_one`, the closed forms `ruin_prob_win_eq`/`ruin_prob_lose_eq`, and positivity/strict-bound lemmas.
sections.mathContext: Optional Stopping on $X_n$ gives $P_{win}=k/N$, with $P_{win}+P_{lose}=1$ and $0<P_{win}<1$.

sections.title: Part III: Expected Ruin Time via the Quadratic Martingale
sections.summary: Uses the quadratic martingale Xₙ²−n: `expected_squared_at_ruin`, `expected_ruin_time_eq` (E[T]=k(N−k)), positivity, and the AM-GM bound `expected_ruin_time_le_quarter_N_sq` (E[T] ≤ N²/4).

sections.title: Part IV: Concrete Examples
sections.summary: Worked instances: `example_5_10` (win prob 1/2, E[T]=25), `example_1_10` (E[T]=9), and `example_1_100` (E[T]=99), each evaluated from the closed forms.

sections.title: Part V: Symmetry and Structural Properties
sections.summary: Structural identities: `expected_ruin_time_symmetric` (E[T|k]=E[T|N−k]), the increment recurrence `expected_ruin_time_increment`, and the discrete `harmonic_property`.
sections.mathContext: $E[T|k]=E[T|N-k]$; expected time satisfies a discrete harmonic/recurrence relation.

sections.title: Part VI: Variance Bounds
sections.summary: Bounds on the squared/second-moment quantities: `expected_time_sq_upper_bound` and the worked values `expected_time_N2_k1`, `expected_time_N4_k2`.
sections.mathContext: Upper bounds on $E[T]^2$/second moments with concrete instances.

sections.title: Part VII: Asymptotic Analysis
sections.summary: `expected_ruin_time_quadratic` (the quadratic growth of E[T] in N) and `poor_gambler_expected_time` (the k=1 'poor gambler' asymptotic E[T]=N−1).

sections.title: Part VIII: Biased Random Walk (p ≠ 1/2)
sections.summary: Introduces `BiasedGamblersRuin` with odds ratio r=q/p and proves the biased ruin probabilities `biasedRuinProbWin`/`biasedRuinProbLose` ((1−rᵏ)/(1−rᴺ)), the sum-to-one identity, the favorable (r<1) and unfavorable (r>1) cases, and `fair_limit_lhopital` recovering the symmetric formula as p→1/2.
sections.mathContext: Biased walk: $P_{win}=(1-r^k)/(1-r^N)$, $r=q/p$; L'Hôpital limit recovers the fair case.

sections.title: Part IX: Exponential Decay of Ruin Time Distribution
sections.summary: The dominant eigenvalue cos(π/N) governs the exponential tail: `ruin_time_decay_rate_pos` and `ruin_time_decay_rate_lt_one` (0 < cos(π/N) < 1 for N ≥ 3), plus `expected_time_from_pgf_agrees` reconciling the PGF derivation with E[T]=k(N−k).

sections.title: Part X: Second Moment and Variance of Ruin Time
sections.summary: Defines `expectedRuinTimeSq`/`varianceRuinTime`, proves `variance_eq_second_moment_minus_square`, the second-moment recurrence and boundary conditions, `variance_nonneg`, `variance_symmetric`, `variance_upper_bound`, the `coefficient_of_variation_sq`, and concrete variance values (N2_k1, N4_k2, N3_k1, N10_k5).
sections.mathContext: Variance of T: $\mathrm{Var}(T)=E[T^2]-E[T]^2$ via a second-moment recurrence, with bounds and worked values.

crossReferences.description: Applies the parent Fair Games Theorem (OST) to the specific setting of symmetric and biased random walks with absorbing barriers
The ballot problem studies first-passage times of random walks, which are stopping times for the martingale of cumulative votes
The CLT governs the distribution of cumulative winnings in fair games; ruin time distributions connect to the tail behavior of random walks
The LLN ensures that average winnings converge to zero in fair games, while this entry studies the distribution of the stopping time (ruin) before convergence

conclusion.summary: A complete axiom-free analysis of the Gambler's Ruin problem, extending from symmetric to biased random walks and establishing the exponential decay rate of the ruin time distribution.
conclusion.implications: The formalization demonstrates that the entire theory of gambler's ruin can be derived from algebraic identities once the OST is available. The biased case reveals dramatic asymmetry: even a tiny house edge makes ruin almost certain.
openQuestions: Can we formalize the full spectral decomposition of the ruin time distribution?
What is the exact variance formula via the quartic martingale?
Can the continuous-time limit (Brownian motion) be formalized?
